newsitem.title: UK: Emerging Europe Advertising & Media Digest - July 8.
newsitem.headline: Emerging Europe Advertising & Media Digest - July 8.

text.p: REUTERS EMERGING EUROPE PRESS DIGEST FOR ADVERTISING & MEDIA
Weekly Press Digest from Central and Eastern Europe on Advertising, Marketing, the Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Markets
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
-- Bulgarian National Television has asked the government to set tariffs and terms for advertising in order to stop speculation about corrupt practices in the industry. (Pari, July 2, 1997)

-- Moscow's GAI road police have set new standards for outdoor advertising, requiring that each site be licensed. As a result, much outdoor advertising will effectively be banned.(Nedelya, weekly supplement to Izvestiya, June 30-July 6, 1997)

-- Czech ad agency Hager Praha has begun a TV, radio, press and poster campaign for Fa Kiwi shower gels and deodorant sprays made by Schwartzkopf & Henkel. The agency has also hired a tram in Prague where passengers will be given free samples of the products. (Strategie News, June 6-July 2, 1997)

-- Grade, a Czech ad agency, has become part of the global advertising group TBWA International. Grade's turnover in 1996 was 260 million crowns ($8.1 million). Its clients include Daewoo Motor, Scholler and KFC. (Strategie News, June 6-July 2, 1997)
-- Saatchi & Saatchi has paid about $350,000 in back taxes and penalties after a tax police raid on its Moscow office, according to Alexander Borisov, a Moscow tax police spokesman.
(Kommersant - Daily, July 1, 1997)

-- Poland's television advertising market will be worth 1.482 billion zlotys ($452.6 million) in 1997 and the gross ad sales of the privately-owned commercial Polsat station will reach 642 million zlotys, according to IP Polska.(Media Polska, July/August, 1997)

-- Czech advertising agency Head 2 has been accepted into E3, an international network of independent agencies. Head 2 is a subsidiary of German Head 2 International Communication & Advertising Network. Its clients include Canon CZ, Teacher's and Vision Express. (Strategie News, June 6-July 2, 1997)
-- The Prague office of Ammirati Puris Lintas has won the Czech advertising account for the German bank, BNP-Dresdner Bank.
(Hospodarske Noviny, July 4, 1997)

-- Poland's major outdoor advertising firms say they have reached an informal agreement that the price for renting outdoor advertising space should not exceed $6 per square metre.(Media Polska, July/August, 1997)

-- The Moscow government plans to place about 10 large television screens, measuring 10x20 metres and 9x13 metres, in central streets. The screens will carry advertising and information about the weather and traffic jams. (Moskovsky Komsomolets, July 3, 1997)
-- The number of advertising billboards in Poland rose 11.24 percent in the first quarter of 1997, according to the EastPlak Polska outdoor ad agency. (Media Polska, July/August, 1997)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

-- Bulgarias parliament is expected to replace the directors of national television and radio, and possibly the director of the state news agency BTA, who were appointed by the previous Socialist-dominated parliament. (Capital, June 30-July 6, 1997)

-- The Bulgarian government is considering different options for privatising national televisions second channel, Prime Minister Ivan Kostov says. He expects the sale to be finalised in October. (Kontinent, July 2, 1997)

-- Petyo Blaskov, the founder and director of Bulgaria's biggest press group, 168 Chasa, is expected to be dismissed from his post by 168 Chasa's German owner, the Westdeutsche Allgemeine Zeitung group, which owns 70 percent of the Bulgarian media.
(Democratsia, July 2, 1997)

-- The Czech Republic's Bureau for Preserving Economic Competition has fined Kabel Plus, a cable company, 500,000 crowns for misusing its dominant position. According to a spokesman for the anti-monopoly office, Kabel Plus was fined for pushing clients to agree to unfair contracts for cable television. (Hospodarske Noviny, June 30, 1997)
-- The Jard-Press press distribution chain says it has launched an on-line news service at a cost of $180,000.(Media Polska, July/August, 1997)
-- Multico holding, which controls Poland's Zycie Warszawy daily, has launched a new Zycie i Kryminal monthly on crime prevention and security measures. (Media Polska, July/August, 1997)

-- The Czech Republic's Council for Radio and Television Broadcasting has begun legal proceedings to revoke the licence of Kaskol, operator of national radio station Radio Alfa, council chairman Bohuslav Hanus says. He says Kaskol has not fulfilled the project and programming conditions of the licence.
(Hospodarske Noviny, July 3, 1997)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
-- Hungarian pharmaceutical companies will not cut their prices despite the abolition of Hungary's import surcharge.
Negotiations over drug prices with the National Healthcare Insurance Fund (OEP) will start on September 15, Hungarian drug firms announced. (Vilaggazdasag, July 2, 1997)

-- Opel Southeast Europe Kft won a contract to sell more than 900 five-door 1.6 Astra cars to the Hungarian police for a total value of 2.5 billion forints ($13.2 million). Magyar Suzuki Rt won a contract worth 520 million forints to sell cars to the Hungarian police. (Vilaggazdasag, July 3, 1997)
-- Masters, a brand of jeans produced by Elpo, a jeans maker in Legnica, in western Poland, is aimed at a young, medium-income market. (Businessman Magazine, July, 1997)
